description:
The DFHPF3 arm at :88-90, which is this program's only EXEC CICS SEND TEXT and its only bare EXEC CICS RETURN. A communication area is present so :80 is false and :85 evaluates EIBAID; the second WHEN of an ordered three-arm EVALUATE matches; :89 moves CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU into WS-MESSAGE; and :90 performs SEND-PLAIN-TEXT, which transmits FROM(WS-MESSAGE) LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-MESSAGE) ERASE FREEKB at :164-169 and then issues EXEC CICS RETURN at :171-172 with no TRANSID and no COMMAREA. The pseudo-conversation therefore ends there and :98-102 is never reached. Note what this arm does not do: it sets no error flag, because signing off is not an error, so WS-ERR-FLG keeps the N it was initialised to at :75; and it never performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, so RECEIVE MAP at :110-115 is never issued and mapFields is empty by derivation rather than by omission.

Why case12 carries this arm. :85-95 is a three-arm ordered EVALUATE - WHEN DFHENTER, WHEN DFHPF3, WHEN OTHER - and every arm needs a case or the ordering is asserted with a hole in it. case12 is the only one of the twenty that presses PF3: case13 presses PF4 and case19 presses CLEAR, and both land on WHEN OTHER, while the remaining seventeen either press ENTER or arrive with no communication area at all. The unconditional FUNCTION UPPER-CASE fold is asserted where it is observable instead - case09 types admin001 and password, both lower case throughout, and reaches COADM01C; case16 isolates the password fold with USER0003 and password; case10 folds mixed case with UsEr0002 and PassWord - so no part of the fold goes unasserted by this case declining to repeat it. Putting a ninth signing-on case here would have duplicated case09 while leaving the PF3 arm with no case at all, so the arm stays here and the fold stays there.

What the fold does, recorded here because this arm is the one place it provably does not happen. :132-134 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI) into both WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID and :135-136 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(PASSWDI) into WS-USER-PWD, both unconditionally and both after END-EVALUATE, so the keyed read at :215 uses RIDFLD(WS-USER-ID) - the folded value, never the bytes as typed - and the plaintext comparison at :223 tests the stored password against the folded password. The three receivers are the only ones: the folded values are never moved back into USERIDI or USERIDO or PASSWDI or PASSWDO. Since app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY declares COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI with the same FILLER X(12) prologue and the same 7 + n stride per field - two length bytes, one flag byte and four filler bytes on the input side against three filler bytes and four attribute bytes on the output side - USERIDO overlays USERIDI byte for byte, so an echoed screen field keeps the raw typed bytes while the communication area carries the folded value. FUNCTION UPPER-CASE folds only a through z and leaves every other byte alone, which is why the digits of a key such as admin002 survive it intact. On this arm none of that runs: EIBAID is PF3, so :108-140 is never entered, nothing is folded, USRSEC is never read and no communication area is handed on. Nothing here may be harmonised with its sibling either: COSGN00C folds unconditionally while COUSR01C, the user-add screen, performs no case normalisation at all - FUNCTION UPPER-CASE occurs twice in app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl and zero times in app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl. Both behaviours coexist in the legacy system and both are preserved exactly as they are.

The eighty-byte line, and the trap inside it. :89 moves CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU, which app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:18-19 declares PIC X(50) VALUE 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...', into the PIC X(80) WS-MESSAGE at :38, so the fifty characters are left-justified and the remaining thirty are spaces - forty-three characters of text then thirty-seven spaces. That sender is not the similarly named CCDA-THANK-YOU of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, which is PIC X(40): the two differ by ten bytes, they are owned by different classes, and only the X(50) one is moved here. The line is pinned on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel because LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-MESSAGE) sends eighty bytes, and this is the only place among this program's twenty cases where the full PIC X(80) WS-MESSAGE is observable rather than the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO projection that :149 produces on every map-sending path. No expectedResponse is pinned at all, and that absence is itself the assertion: SEND TEXT transmits unformatted data rather than a map, so there is no BMS payload to compare, no mapset or map to name, no navigation context handed on and no termination to state. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO is not performed on this path either, so no header field is composed and no ERRMSG is set.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then the named SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and never hand-padded, and the 80-character expectedFinalState images prove that span was emitted as 23 spaces - a record missing it would be short by exactly 23. Row 1, the ADMIN002 row, additionally names all six fields individually so those offsets are diffable against the copybook rather than inferred from one long string; note that its first and last name are both RUSSELL, which is the seed data as the job writes it and not a transcription slip. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 - and never by a dataset name. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not even specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedReturnCode is 0 because a grep for RETURN-CODE over the program counts 0.

Determinism and the two substitutions. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so wherever the clock is read it is pinned rather than sampled: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it. This arm never reaches that paragraph, so the instant is declared for consistency with the other nineteen cases and nothing on this path consumes it. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds, so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(08) are pinned constants standing in for those two calls; all twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated rather than hidden. The charset is named US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default. There is no randomness and no wall-clock reading anywhere in this case.

Security posture, unchanged in both directions. SEC-USR-PWD is PIC X(08) and app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:223 compares it in plaintext, so the seeded PASSWORD stays plaintext here: no digest is computed over it, no random prefix is mixed into it, no credential transformer is applied to it, no bearer credential is minted from it and no security filter chain exists anywhere in this file. The fold at :135-136 is applied to the password as well as to the user id, which narrows the effective password space, since a password containing lower-case letters can never be stored and matched as typed. That is an inherited property of the legacy design, preserved deliberately and not endorsed, and correcting either of them would be a behaviour change rather than a migration.

Two absences worth stating so that neither is read as an oversight. app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7 - a COBOL comment - so no DFHATTR constant applies to this program even though the symbolic map carries attribute items; and COSGN00C never copies CSSETATY, so there is no DFHRED-plus-asterisk runtime highlight to assert on any path, this one included. The red on the error line is a static map property assembled once from app/bms/COSGN00.bms rather than assigned at run time, and this arm paints no map at all.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy and app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the literals and the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: a grep for GO TO and a grep for CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl both count 0, and neither is faked. DUPKEY, DUPREC and ENDFILE are unreachable from this program, and none of them is invented here.
